title: How to send Shopify orders to Google Sheets | 50agents
description: Send Shopify orders to Google Sheets with Shopify Flow or an automation: choose one row per order or per item first, then catch cancellations too.
h1: How to send Shopify orders to Google Sheets
answer: Use Shopify Flow’s "Add row to spreadsheet" action (free on every Shopify plan) or an automation tool that adds a row on each new order, after deciding whether you want one row per order or one row per item.
Then add a second step for cancelled orders, because a new-order trigger never touches the row again when an order is edited or cancelled.

sections.h2: First decide: one row per order, or one per item

body.p: This one choice decides everything after it. Answer it from what you will do with the sheet.

head: One row per order
One row per item
rows: Revenue by day, order counts, shipping
Best sellers, stock planning, variant sales
Order number, date, customer, items as text, total
Order number, date, product, variant, SKU, quantity, line price
Order totals repeat across rows; never SUM them
Wrap "Add row" in For each over the line items

body.p: Shopify’s own CSV export already puts extra line items on their own rows with most fields left blank. If you only need a monthly view, that export may be all you need.

head: Way

rows: By hand. Up to 50 orders download at once; bigger exports are emailed to you.
Free on Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus
Row contents are comma-separated, so a comma in a product name splits the row; Shopify suggests a Liquid replace filter.
Pick "new order" or "order paid" on purpose; one includes unpaid orders, the other does not.

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: Build the header row
steps.body: Order number first, then date, customer, the columns from your choice above, and a Status column. Freeze the header.

steps.title: Pick the trigger
steps.body: New order catches every order, paid or not; order paid catches only money in. In viaSocket’s catalog Shopify has "New Order", "Order Paid" and "Order Cancelled" as triggers.

steps.title: Map line items deliberately
steps.body: For one row per order, join items into one cell ("2 x Oat Latte Blend, 1 x Grinder"). For one row per item, loop over the line items and repeat the order number on each row.

steps.title: Clean the text
steps.body: Strip commas and line breaks from product names and notes, or quote them, so columns stay in place.

steps.title: Catch cancellations
steps.body: A second automation on "Order Cancelled" finds the order number in the sheet and sets Status to Cancelled. Do the same for refunds if you report on them.

steps.title: Test with a real order
steps.body: Place a test order with two products, one with a comma in its name, then cancel it. You should see one or two rows, then a Cancelled status.

body: Here is the one-row-per-order version as Captain builds it in 50agents. It reads a real order from your store to plan the columns, tests the steps on that order, and keeps the automation as a draft until you tap Make it live.

wrong.title: Edited orders leave old numbers
wrong.body: Shopify lets you add or remove items and change quantities after an order is placed. A new-order trigger never sees that. Add an update step, or treat the sheet as a log and reconcile from Shopify monthly.

wrong.title: Duplicate rows
wrong.body: Shopify retries webhooks up to 8 times over 4 hours when your endpoint does not answer within 5 seconds. Look the order number up before adding.

wrong.title: Columns shift
wrong.body: A comma or a line break in a product name or note splits the row. Clean the text first.

wrong.title: Only paid orders arrived
wrong.body: You picked "order paid" but wanted cash-on-delivery orders too. Switch to new order and keep a Status column.

wrong.title: Totals counted twice
wrong.body: With one row per item, the order total repeats on every row. Sum line prices instead.

wrong.title: The sheet slows down
wrong.body: Google Sheets holds up to 20 million cells, but a sheet full of formulas gets slow far sooner. Start a new tab each year.

faqs.q: Can Shopify export orders straight to Google Sheets?
faqs.a: Not live from the Orders page, which exports CSV files. Shopify Flow’s "Add row to spreadsheet" action can write each order into a Google Sheet as it arrives.
Yes, on Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus. Its "Send HTTP request" action needs Grow or above, but adding sheet rows does not.

faqs.q: How do I get one row per product?
faqs.a: Loop over the order’s line items and add a row for each, repeating the order number. In Flow that is the For each step around Add row.
